Inch is also the name of the civil parish covering the island.


== Geography and history ==
Inch Island is around 13 square kilometres (5 sq mi) in area. The island lies in Lough Swilly, Inch being just off the south-western coast of the Inishowen mainland, near the village of Burt. Inch Island is connected to the mainland by a causeway road, known as the Inch Banks. The island's highest hill, Inch Top, is 222 metres in height. Another Irish language name for Inch Island is Inis na nOsirí, meaning 'Island of the Oysters'.


== Population ==

The table reports data taken from Discover the Islands of Ireland (Alex Ritsema, Collins Press, 1999) and the Census of Ireland.


== Buildings ==

The remains of a portal tomb with a nearby burial chamber, probably constructed using parts of the original tomb, is located near Carnaghan (Irish: Baile Mhic Cearnachain) on the south-western part of the island.
A 15th century castle, known as Inch Castle, stands on a cliff overlooking Lough Swilly.
